描述_EN: camels and horses were used as pack animals and merchants passed their goods from oasis to oasis. the victoria and albert museum has around 700 ancient and medieval textiles recovered by stein at the beginning of the twentieth century. the most notable item traded was silk. the site is part of an area now referred to as the silk road, a series of overland trade routes that crossed asia, from china to europe. the silk road was also important for the exchange of ideas – while silk textiles travelled west from china, buddhism entered china from india in this way. it was intended for use as a burial face cover. it was recovered from the site of astana, an ancient burial ground dating from the 3rd to the 8th century ad. some are silk while others are made from the wool of a variety of different animals. this textile is of patterned weave silk and shows the remains of a boar in orange and black. the textiles range in date from the second century bc to the twelfth century ad. the fragments were brought back from central asia by the explorer and archaeologist sir marc aurel stein (1862–1943).
描述_ZN: 年，骆驼和马被用作驮运动物，商人们在绿洲之间传递他们的货物。 年，维多利亚和阿尔伯特博物馆有大约700件古代和中世纪的纺织品，是斯坦在20世纪初找到的。 年，最引人注目的贸易项目是丝绸。 年：该遗址是现在被称为 "丝绸之路 "的地区的一部分，这是一系列横跨亚洲、从中国到欧洲的陆上贸易路线。 年：丝绸之路对思想交流也很重要--当丝绸纺织品从中国向西运输时，佛教也通过这种方式从印度进入中国。 它的目的是作为一个埋葬的面罩。 它是在阿斯塔纳遗址中发现的，这是一个可以追溯到公元3世纪到8世纪的古墓葬地。 有些是丝绸，有些则是由各种不同动物的羊毛制成。 这块纺织品是花纹编织的丝绸，显示了一头野猪的橙色和黑色的残骸。 这些纺织品的年代从公元前二世纪到公元十二世纪不等。 这些碎片是由探险家和考古学家Marc Aurel Stein先生（1862-1943）从亚洲中部带回来的。
